question: Which of the following molecules is diatomic in nature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Oxygen (O₂)** is a diatomic molecule, meaning it consists of two oxygen atoms.
 
• It is the most abundant element in the Earth's atmosphere, making up about 21% by volume.
 
• Oxygen is essential for respiration in most living organisms and is also crucial for combustion processes.
 
• In its diatomic form, oxygen is a colorless, odorless gas at room temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diatomic Molecules:**

 
 
• Diatomic molecules are molecules composed of only two atoms, of the same or different chemical elements.
 
• Common diatomic molecules include hydrogen (H₂), nitrogen (N₂), oxygen (O₂), fluorine (F₂), and chlorine (Cl₂).
 
 
 
• **Oxygen's Role in Life:**
 
 
• Oxygen is vital for cellular respiration, a process by which cells produce energy.
 
• It is also used in medical treatments, such as oxygen therapy for patients with respiratory issues.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen in Industrial Use:**
 
 
• Oxygen is used in various industrial processes including steelmaking, welding, and as an oxidizer in rocket fuel.
 
• It is also used in water treatment and chemical manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes of Oxygen:**
 
 
• There are three stable isotopes of oxygen: O-16, O-17, and O-18, with O-16 being the most abundant.
 
• These isotopes are used in scientific research, including climate studies and paleoclimatology.
